correctness.rationale: Synchronous noisy-voter transition matrices on finite P_n are strictly positive because any configuration can be obtained by all-site refresh, giving a unique stationary law and almost-sure time-frequency ergodic convergence. Backward copying genealogy gives agreement 1/2 plus half the coalescence probability. Two-step return is c²/2 and a second term c²/2 E[c^{2σ_n}] from two walks starting at 0,2. Folding independent Z-walks to reflecting path produces an exact walk Z=((A+B)/2,(A−B)/2) from (1,−1), with four compass moves; the first simultaneous meeting is first exit from (0,n−1)×(−(n−1),0). Nested rectangles give τ_{n−1}≤τ_{m−1} pathwise and the all-east event provides a positive quantitative difference for every c∈(0,1). n=2 is handled separately. I independently solved exact rational square-exit resolvents at c=3/5 for n=3..7 and obtained strict decreasing h_n; read verify.py finite-state, pair-walk and square-resolvent checkers.

value.rationale: Endpoint-rooted paths form the natural first unresolved branching-one boundary of existing noisy-voter reconstruction. Strict ordering at every positive noise, with an explicit quantitative separation and exact random-walk representation, is a useful structural identification theorem; not a routine consequence of ergodicity.
